banner.title: fstrim
banner.tagline: Once a week, discards unused blocks on every node's block mounts, so thin Ceph RBD volumes give back their space.

art.about: a weekly job that enters the host mount namespace and discards unused blocks
art.title: How fstrim reclaims Ceph space

explainer.title: From a Monday cron to a discard on every device

steps.title: Schedule
steps.text: CronJob fstrim runs Mondays at 00:00 with one pod per node. A run never overlaps the last, and a start more than 10 minutes late is skipped.
steps.scene: a wall clock above a weekly calendar tick

steps.title: Enter
steps.text: Each pod uses nsenter to join the kubelet's mount and network namespaces through /host/proc, so it sees the mounts that Ceph PVs live in.
steps.scene: a key sliding into a host namespace ring

steps.title: Select
steps.text: awk reads mountinfo, keeps one mount per device (globalmount first), and skips read-only mounts and sources that are not under /dev.
steps.scene: stacked disk layers passing through a funnel

steps.title: Trim
steps.text: fstrim -v runs on each target. Any device that fails fails the run. A mount that vanished mid-run is skipped, not counted as a failure.
steps.scene: a block of disk cells being wiped clean

steps.title: Watch
steps.text: FstrimJobFailed fires when the latest run failed or no run has succeeded for 8 days, and clears on the next good run.
steps.scene: a bell over a calendar with one date unmarked
